question: Should OpenClaw adopt this Discord subagent-progress feature and its permanent requester-message, channel-lifecycle, and configuration contracts?
rationale: Tests and live proof can validate the implementation, but they cannot decide whether this cross-boundary API and seven-field operator surface are the product contract maintainers want to support.

options.title: Sponsor a generic lifecycle contract
options.body: Approve the feature direction, confirm the smallest generic core/SDK seam, keep Discord behavior plugin-owned, and require a clean rebase plus exact-head proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the public surface
options.body: Keep the Discord capability but rework the branch to avoid or reduce the new channel lifecycle API and configuration knobs before reconsidering merge.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Close or pause the PR if permanent source-message progress semantics are not currently worth the core lifecycle and compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a generic lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Approve the feature direction, confirm the smallest generic core/SDK seam, keep Discord behavior plugin-owned, and require a clean rebase plus exact-head proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice primarily concerns Agents and Hooks contracts, which repository ownership guidance assigns to this person.
